# APPENDIX: STEAM TANK RULES

*Pages PDF 21-31*

THE EMPEROR’S WRATH 

## Appendix: Steam Tank Rules
This section provides rules for operating a Steam Tank, and how to reduce one to scrap. 

## **Basic Operations Manual**
The first step in learning to pilot a Steam Tank is coaxing the boiler’s steam pressure to propel locomotive systems. Outside of battle this is far less taxing, but never without risk, even for veteran engineers. 

## **Steam Tank Capacity**
The interior of a Steam Tank is extremely cramped, but if all occupants are cooperating to share the space, it can fit up to five Characters of Size Medium or smaller. Five additional Size Medium Characters can ride atop the Steam Tank’s exterior. 

If the Steam Tank is without a turret, only four Size Medium Characters can fit inside the Steam Tank, but six Size Medium Characters can ride on top of it. 

Despite their formidable locomotive power, Steam Tanks are rarely used to transport cargo, to avoid placing stress upon their delicate systems. If obliged to do so, a Steam Tank can transport 2 Encumbrance inside the vehicle (usually Trade Tools and replacement components), and up to 50 Encumbrance on top of it. 

## **Steam Tank Systems**
Whilst inside a Steam Tank, a Character has access to the following systems: 

Locomotion (for driving the Steam Tank). 

Weaponry (for operating one of the Steam Tank’s weapons, as a gunner or loader). 

Engineering (for working the Steam Tank’s boiler to build up Steam Points). 

Each of these Steam Tank systems can only be used once per combat round, even if multiple Characters are operating the system. The exceptions are the Steam Tank’s weapons, each of which can only be fired once per round but can be loaded by any number of Characters whether the weapon fired that round or not. 

During combat, swapping places with an allied Character operating a different Steam Tank system, or taking up position beside an unoccupied Steam Tank system, requires a Character to use their Move for the turn. 

## **Travel Speed**
Undertaking a journey aboard a Steam Tank requires at least one Character to have Advances in the Trade (Engineering) Advanced Skill and fulfil the role of engineer commander. Whilst so occupied, a Steam Tank can move at a speed equivalent to the walking speed for a Character with M of 4, for up to 12 hours, without placing undue stress upon its boiler. Steam Tanks may not run. After every 12 hours of travel, the engineer commander must make a **Challenging (+0) Trade (Engineering)** Test. If they fail, the vehicle suffers a Steam Tank Mishap (see below). 

When time is of the essence, a Steam Tank can move up to five times this speed, assuming the engineer commander can manage to regulate the boiler pressure. After an hour of moving at accelerated speed, the Steam Tank commander must succeed on a **Challenging (+0) Trade (Engineering)** Test, or the vehicle suffers a Steam Tank Mishap. The difficulty of this Test increases to **Difficult (–10)** if moving the equivalent of M 5–6, **Hard (–20)** if moving M 7–8, or **Very Hard (–30)** if moving M 9–10. Again, these Movement scores only relate to walking speed; Steam Tanks may not run. 

If a single Character is operating a Steam Tank as both driver and engineer commander, the vehicle’s maximum movement speeds listed above are reduced. In this case the difficulty of this Test increases to **Difficult (–10)** if moving the equivalent of M 5, **Hard (–20)** if moving M 6, or **Very Hard (–30)** if moving M 7. Again, these Movement scores only relate to walking speed; Steam Tanks may not run. 

Difficult terrain and bad weather can also slow a Steam Tank’s travel speed, though some environments obstructive to travellers on foot (such as light foliage and urban ruins) can be demolished by a Steam Tank without slowing down. 

## **Steam Tank Mishaps**
A Steam Tank suffers Mishaps from battle damage or system stress. When prompted, roll a d100, and consult the chart one page 22 for the Mishap’s effects. Note that Mishap effects which injure all Characters inside the Steam Tank also injure Characters riding on top of it. For this reason, warriors do not usually ride atop a Steam Tank once battle begins! 

## **Mishap Table**
|D100 Roll|Effect|
|---|---|
|01-24|Out of Control|
|25-49|LeakingSteam|
|50-74|Overheating|
|75-94|Weapon Disabled|
|95-99|Immobilised|

## **Out of Control**
A rocking jolt shakes the Steam Tank, and its locomotion systems jerk into overdrive. At the start of the driver’s turn (or at the end of the turn, if no Character is occupying the locomotion systems), the Steam Tank spends all available Steam Points to move in a direction of the GM’s choosing. GMs are encouraged to sadistically direct the Steam Tank towards an unbreakable obstacle, towards unsuspecting allies, away from support, or over a cliff edge. If the Steam Tank has no Steam Points when making this involuntarily movement, it instead grinds its gears, and suffers an additional Steam Tank Mishap (re-roll additional Out of Control results). The driver cannot move the Steam Tank of their own accord until they spend an Action and succeed on a **Challenging (+0) Drive** Test. 

## **Leaking Steam**
The Steam Tank’s pipes violently vent a thin, uncontrolled stream of water vapour from out of the closed system. A random Character inside the tank suffers +d10 Damage from the sudden discharge, reduced by Toughness and Armour. At the end of each combat round, the Steam Tank loses 1 Steam Point per Leaking Steam Mishap. When moving outside combat, the tank reduces its speed 1 mph per Leaking Steam Mishap suffered. Repairing a Leaking Steam Mishap requires an hour of work and a successful **Challenging (+0) Trade (Engineering)** Test. 

## **Overheating**
The boiler buckles against its restraints, and scorching water gushes from the container, suffocating the tank’s occupants in a cloud of steam. Every Character aboard the tank suffers +d10 Damage, reduced by Toughness and Armour. The Steam Tank’s Maximum Pressure 

(see page 23) is reduced by 1 per Overheating Mishap. When moving outside combat, the tank reduces its speed 1 mph per Overheating Mishap suffered. Repairing an Overheating Mishap requires an hour of work and a successful **Challenging (+0) Trade (Engineering)** Test. 

## **Weapon Disabled**
The pipes connecting one of the Steam Tank’s weapons to the boiler shears off. Choose one of the Steam Tank’s operational weapons at random. Every Character operating the weapon as a gunner or loader suffers +d10 Damage from the steam backwash, reduced by Toughness and Armour. The weapon becomes unusable until the Mishap is repaired, which requires 12 hours of work and a successful **Challenging (+0) Trade (Engineering)** Test. If the Steam Tank does not have any operational weapons when this Mishap is rolled, re-roll until you receive a different Steam Tank Mishap. 

## **Immobilised**
The pistons that turn the Steam Tank’s wheels explode, bringing the vehicle to a screeching halt as its prow buries itself in the dirt. Every Character operating the Steam Tank’s locomotive and engineering systems suffers +d10 Damage from the blast of searing vapour, reduced by Toughness and Armour. Whilst Immobilised, the vehicle cannot move, and any Out of Control and Immobilised results on the Mishap table are re-rolled. Repairing this Mishap usually requires days of work in a dedicated workshop, but ingenious engineers may juryrig a solution in the field. 

## **Meltdown**
The pressure on the boiler proves unsustainable, resulting in a catastrophic explosion that douses the crew in boiling water. All Characters aboard the Steam Tank suffer +2d10 Damage, reduced by Toughness and Armour. The vehicle’s Steam Points are reset to 0, and the Steam Tank’s systems can neither generate nor spend Steam Points. The vehicle is Wrecked (see page 27), and must be returned to an engineering workshop before it can be repaired. 

## **Tank Combat**
Steam Tanks do not take their own actions in combat, but Characters crewing the vehicle can use its systems on their turn: to manage the boiler pressure, drive the tank forward, and fire its assortment of artillery. 

## **Steam Points**
To move a Steam Tank and use its weapons in combat, the vehicle must spend Steam Points, which are built up within the steam boiler and directed to relevant systems. If at the start of combat a Character with Advances in the 

THE EMPEROR’S WRATH 

Trade (Engineering) Skill is operating the vehicle’s boiler, that Character may choose how many Steam Points the vehicle begins with. Otherwise the vehicle begins combat with 0 Steam Points. 

Steam Tanks have a Maximum Pressure rating, which determines the highest number of Steam Points the Steam Tank can store without suffering a Mishap. By default, a Steam Tank’s Maximum Pressure is 10. Mishaps or modifications can affect this rating. 

Steam Points can drop below 0 (into negative numbers) and have no upper limit (they can exceed the tank’s Maximum Pressure). However, if during a Character’s turn a vehicle’s Steam Points are reduced below 0, or become higher than the tank’s Maximum Pressure rating, it immediately rolls for a Steam Tank Mishap. A Steam Tank also suffers a Mishap if, at the start of a combat round, its Steam Points are lower than 0, or higher than the tank’s Maximum Pressure rating. 

## **Working the Boiler**
Once per round, a Character operating the Steam Tank’s engineering systems can spend an Action to adjust the boiler pressure. Before making their Test, the Character must declare exactly how many Steam Points they want the vehicle to gain or lose. 

Increasing the number of Steam Points is a **Challenging (+0) Trade (Engineering)** Test. Decreasing the number of Steam Points is an **Average (+20) Trade (Engineering)** Test. 

If the Test succeeds, the vehicle gains the number of Steam Points specified. If the Test generates positive SLs, the Character may optionally choose to increase or decrease the Steam Point adjustment beyond what they originally specified, so long as the value of this adjustment does not exceed the number of SLs generated. 

If the Test fails, the Character still adjusts the number of Steam Points, but the value of this adjustment is modified by the number of negative SLs generated. GMs may choose to increase or decrease the amount of Steam Points generated, so long as the value of their adjustment does not exceed the number of negative SLs generated. Tests which fail but generate 0 negative SLs are assumed to generate 1 negative SL for purposes of this adjustment. 

No matter how badly the Test fails, an attempt to increase Steam Points can never result in a net reduction of Steam Points, and an attempt to decrease Steam Points can never result in a net increase of Steam Points. Enough negative 

SLs can however reduce the effects of the Action to 0 Steam Points gained or lost. 

As usual, if a Character working the boiler adjusts the vehicle’s Steam Points so they are less than 0, or greater than the Maximum Pressure rating, it suffers a Steam Tank Mishap. 

## **Combat Movement**
Once per round, a Character operating the Steam Tank’s locomotion systems can spend Steam Points to move the vehicle as an Action. The driver declares how many Steam Points are being to spent to move the vehicle; they cannot choose to spend more Steam Points than the vehicle currently has. 

For each Steam Point spent, the vehicle moves 3 yards directly forward. After each section of 3 yard movement, the driver may choose to rotate the vehicle 45 degrees in either direction. Alternatively, for each Steam Point spent, the vehicle can move 2 yards directly backwards, and the driver can choose to rotate the vehicle 45 degrees after every 2 yards reversed. 

If driving through terrain that impedes the Steam Tank’s movement, such as marshland, the Steam Tank’s speed is halved. GMs may rule that many inanimate obstacles, such as fences, walls, and foliage, can simply be demolished by the Steam Tank as it moves through without slowing. 

If a Steam Tank is driven through any enemy Characters as part of this movement, the driver resolves a melee attack against each target. This is an **Opposed Drive/Dodge** Test — the driver makes a single Drive Test that applies against all targets, but each defender Tests to Dodge separately. If the defender succeeds, they avoid the Steam Tank’s rampage. If the defender fails, they suffer Damage as usual, with the Steam Tank’s Weapon Damage rated at +10. Because Steam Tanks have Enormous Size, this Damage may gain Qualities or be multiplied per the rules for Size (see **WFRP** , page 341). Attackers do not gain or lose Advantage during a ramming Action, and do not have to Disengage to leave a rammed Character’s melee range. 

Whilst multiple Characters can be attacked as part of a Steam Tank’s movement, a single Character can only be targeted once per turn. If a Character would be impacted multiple times, all subsequent attacks are assumed to be dodged without Testing. 

If a Steam Tank drives into an ally (most likely due to the Out of Control Mishap), the target is attacked as above, except the driver does not Test themself. Instead, the attack is assumed to automatically score 0 SLs. If the defender’s Dodge Test also scores 0 SLs, ties are resolved in the defender’s favour. 

enjoying the benefit of hard cover (–30 to Tests made to target them with missiles) from any return attacks. However, if a Character standing within the turret hatch is incapacitated, enemies who climb atop the Steam Tank (a Challenging (+0) Athletics Test) can attack crew inside the tank directly through the open hatch. 

## **Using Steam Tank Weapons**
The Emperor’s Wrath is equipped with a Helblaster trigun (main weapon) and a steam gun (turret weapon). Any Character operating a weapon can attack with it, though each weapon can only be used to attack once per combat round. All Steam Tank weapons belong to the Ranged (Engineering) group. 

Firing a Steam Tank’s main weapon costs 4 Steam Points. Firing a Steam Tank’s turret weapon costs 2 Steam Points. A gunner cannot choose to use a Steam Tank weapon if attacking would reduce the vehicle to below 0 Steam Points. 

As part of making an attack with a turret weapon, the turret can be turned to face in any direction. Main weapons can only be fired at targets directly in front of the Steam Tank. 

## **Opening the Top Hatch**
A Character who appears from the top hatch may spend a Move in future turns to climb back inside and close the hatch. 

## **Steam Tank Weapons**
Steam Tank weapons are all large and powerful, but their operation is dependent on pressurised steam- and/ or water-driven systems integral to the Steam Tank on which they are fitted. As such they cannot be used if removed from the Steam Tank, or if the boiler of the Steam Tank is not operational. 

Because they are designed to be carried about upon a Steam Tank these weapons are often lighter and shorter than serious artillery weapons of the same type, and the range and force of projectiles fired by such weapons is less than optimal. 

Note: Steam Tank weapons must use special ammunition as detailed in the table below. 

A Character inside a Steam Tank may spend a Move to open the hatch on top of the turret and climb halfway out. From this position, a Character can make an attack with any ranged weapons they are carrying, whilst

## **Helblaster Tri-Gun**
The Helblaster tri-gun has three separate barrels fixed on a circular crank. As the crank is turned, a clever system of cams ignites each charge in turn, propelling a flurry of lethal projectiles from the gun. The advantage of the Helblaster is that it can fire several shots at once in a devastating volley. A full volley will rip through the toughest regiments, causing immense casualties in the blink of an eye. A disadvantage is that it is inclined to jam or misfire, and once it has misfired it is almost always useless until repaired. The chances of being able to fire for a prolonged time are slim, as the weapon is quite likely to malfunction given the complexity of its firing mechanism. 

## **Steam-Powered Cannons**
The largest cannons are restricted to fortresses or wellprepared battlefield positions, but small and medium weapons can be mounted on boats or wagons. On battlefields, cannonballs inflict Damage on ranks of troops by bouncing through them. Given that most combat situations in **Warhammer Fantasy Roleplay** will be smaller skirmishes, the _Blast 2_ Quality is used to represent Damage to those nearby, but if targets are arranged in a line the GM should consider that the ball could conceivably hit multiple consecutive targets. 

## **Mortars**
A mortar is the blackpowder equivalent of a catapult, firing a heavy ball or bomb in a high arc. On the battlefield, they are used mainly in sieges, throwing explosives over castle walls. 

## **Steam Gun**
A steam gun vents super-heated water from the tank’s boiler in an arcing spray. The attacker designates a single target within 20 yards. All Characters within 5 yards of the target, or between the Steam Tank and the target, are struck. The attacker Tests against each struck Character with an **Opposed Ranged (Engineering)/Dodge** Test — the attacker rolls once, and compares their result to each defender in turn. Each defender who fails to Dodge suffers +6 Damage, modified by the attack’s SL and the defender’s Toughness Bonus, but ignoring deductions from AP. Attackers do not generate or lose Advantage when making an attack with a steam gun.

## **New Weapon Qualities or Flaws**
## **Crewed**
A weapon with the _Crewed_ Flaw is so large, heavy, and complex that it benefits from being managed by a team rather than a single operator. This team all need to possess the relevant Ranged Skill to crew the weapon. However, they may nominate one of their number to make the relevant Ranged Test to see how well the weapon performs. 

Most weapons have a crew of 2, 3 or 4. Larger crews are often assembled, but extraneous crew members do not impact the efficiency of the weapon itself, though they may help move it or make up for casualties among the crew. 

If a weapon requiring a crew is not fully crewed it is impaired as explained in the table below. 

When reloading a weapon with the _Crewed_ Flaw, one of the crew may assist with any Tests made to determine how long the reloading process takes. 

If a weapon with the _Crewed_ Flaw suffers a misfire, all members of the crew are affected. 

_**Example:** Von Meinkop is trying to fire a Steam-Powered Cannon without the assistance of any additional crew. Von Meinkop can use his impressive Ranged (Engineering) Skill of 92 to fire the weapon. However, because he is the sole crew member of a Crewed 4 weapon, it doubles the reload time (from 8 to 16) and gains the_ Imprecise _Flaw. The weapon ought to also gain the_ Dangerous _Flaw, but it already has this Flaw, so Von Meinkop’s Ranged (Engineering) suffers a penalty of –10 when shooting the cannon._ 

## **Salvo**
Penalties from reduced crew are cumulative, so a _Crewed 4_ weapon with a single crewperson will suffer from double reload time, the _Imprecise_ Flaw, and the _Dangerous_ Flaw. 

If a weapon gains a Flaw that it already possesses, impose a further penalty of –10 to any Ranged Tests made to shoot the weapon. 

A weapon with the _Salvo_ Quality has the potential to launch missiles either one at a time or in batches. The number of times the weapon can be fired is indicated by the Salvo number. Each time the weapon is fired reduce the Salvo number by 1. The weapon does not need to be reloaded until it reaches Salvo 0.

A _Salvo_ weapon can be fired more than once in a turn, but each time the weapon is fired after the first firing, impose a cumulative penalty of –10 to the Ranged Skill used to shoot with the weapon. 

If the weapon misfires at any point in the process, work out the effect of the misfire and then roll on the following table. 

Example: The crew of a Helstorm Rocket Battery benefit from its _Salvo 9_ Quality. Potentially, they could fire the weapon nine times in a single turn. The first turn, they shoot the weapon four times. The first shot is resolved with the Ranged (Engineering) Skill of the nominated crew member. The second shot is resolved with a penalty of –10 to the Ranged (Engineering) Skill of the nominated crew member. The third is resolved with a penalty of –20, and the fourth with a penalty of –30. 

The following turn, the crew fire the weapon five times. This is worked in the same way as the previous turn, but the fifth shot is resolved with a penalty of –40 to the Ranged (Engineering) Skill. The weapon is now empty and must be reloaded before being fired again. 

## **Battling Against a Steam Tank**
Steam Tanks are cacophonous, smog-belching monstrosities of industrial warfare, the likes of which are rarely seen in the Old World. They cause _Terror 1_ in all enemies who confront one in combat. 

If an enemy can overcome their fear, they may attempt to destroy a Steam Tank. Attacking a Steam Tank is resolved like an attack against a Character, except a Character operating the Steam Tank’s locomotion systems defends against melee attacks using their Drive Skill. If no-one is operating the Steam Tank’s locomotion systems when it is attacked in melee, or if the Steam Tank is attacked by a Character who successfully boarded the vehicle with a **Challenging (+0) Athletics** Test, the Steam Tank counts as automatically scoring –10 SL on its Drive Test. 

Because Steam Tanks have Enormous Size, ranged attacks against them gain a +40 modifier, and melee attacks against them by Characters of Size Large or smaller gain a +10 modifier. 

If a Steam Tank is reduced to 0 Wounds, it is Wrecked. It cannot use or generate Steam Points and is functionally unusable until it is returned to an engineering workshop for repairs. 

In addition, if a Steam Tank suffers 20 or more Wounds from a single attack (after deductions from its Toughness Bonus), or if it would suffer a Critical Wound on an attack that inflicted at least 1 Wound, it must immediately roll on the **Steam Tank Mishaps** table (see page 21). 

As part of an attack against a Steam Tank, an attacker may make a called shot (–20 attack modifier), to single out a vulnerable target. If a called shot attack successfully inflicts a Steam Tank Mishap, apply the additional effects below, corresponding to the targeted component: 

- Wheels: If you roll a Weapon Disabled Mishap, count it as an Immobilised Mishap instead. 

- Weapon (choose one): If you roll an Out of Control or Immobilised Mishap, count it as a Weapon Disabled Mishap instead. 

- Rear Boiler: If you roll a Leaking Steam or Overheating Mishap, count it as applying the same Mishap twice. 

- External Access (top hatch or side door): Instead of rolling for a Steam Tank Mishap, the attack destroys the access panel, allowing other enemies to make attacks against the Steam Tank’s crew directly. 

## **Repairing a Steam Tank**
Outside of combat, a Character can make a **Challenging (+0) Trade (Engineer)** Test to repair a Steam Tank as long as they have access to relevant materials and tools. A repair Test takes one hour, with successful Tests restoring (1d10+SL) Wounds. 

Each Steam Tank Mishap (see page 21) provides guidance 

for how to undo its negative effects. 

If a Steam Tank is Wrecked, the vehicle must be towed to an engineering workshop to undergo repairs. For purposes of transportation whilst Wrecked, a Steam Tank has an Encumbrance rating of 450. 

For purposes of absorbing Damage, Steam Tanks have 80 Toughness (reducing all incoming Damage by their Toughness Bonus of 8), and 80 Wounds. Steam Tanks do not have Hit Locations and have special rules for resolving Critical Wounds (see below). 

## **Improving on Genius**
The engineers of the Empire are tinkerers by nature, and every Steam Tank in their care has been modified countless times over its long, glorious history. Where possible, these alterations are undertaken with great care inside the School’s extensive workshop facilities in Altdorf — arranging for modifications is less a matter of expense or engineering skill than a social challenge to secure consent from the School’s leadership. However, circumstances may force Characters to modify a Steam Tank ‘in the field’, which will surely require tools, materials, and an Extended **Trade (Engineering)** Test, assuming it is possible at all. 

## **Reinforced Prow**
This crude weapon, little more than a glorified battering ram, is typically only used when all available steam-power artillery has been destroyed or run out of ammunition. Nonetheless, it has a celebrated history, first adopted by Leonardo’s favourite student Heinrich Woolendurst centuries ago. Nowadays, this variant of Steam Tank is known as the Sigmar’s Hammer, after the most recent Steam Tank to adopt the configuration. 

Steam Tanks with a reinforced prow gain +10 Toughness, and increase the Weapon Damage for ramming attacks to +12. 

The alternate Steam Tank load-outs listed below can be used for making modifications to the Emperor’s Wrath, or to represent the configurations of other Steam Tanks listed on pages 4-5. 

## **Main Weapon Modifications**
Aside from swivel guns,which are mounted to the sides, each of these weapons replaces the Helblaster tri-gun installed on the Emperor’s Wrath by default. Steam cannons and steam mortars are described in the table on page 25. 

## **Swivel Guns**
If a Steam Tank is open-topped, it may install two guns atop its side barriers, as an additional form of antipersonnel protection. Unlike other main weapons, swivel guns do not cost Steam Points to fire, do not replace the Steam Tank’s existing main weapon, and can be turned to fire in any direction. 

## **Turret Modifications**
Each of these modifications alters the top of the Steam Tank, where the steam gun turret of the Emperor’s Wrath is usually installed.

## **Bazalgette Gun-Ring**
Properly known as ‘Bazalgette’s exalted-velocity fusillade of ultra-rotary unleashment’, this extraordinarily impractical weapon consists of a circular mount with 24 handguns in concentric circles, all fired within seconds by turning a crank which spins the firing mechanism. Its devastating rate of fire cannot compensate for its appalling reload time, but the maverick engineers under Baron von Helsing labour tirelessly to devise a solution. Bazalgette gun-rings use the profile of a handgun ( **WFRP** , page 295), with the _Blast 2_ , _Impact_ (replaces Damaging), _Repeater 2_ , and _Reload 12_ (replaces _Reload 3_ ) Qualities and Flaws. 

## **Remove Turret**
A Steam Tank’s turret may be removed to reduce its weight, remove a target for boarders, or improve its exterior transport capacity (at the cost of interior transport capacity — see page 21 for details). 

## **Fighting Platform**
Inspired by the design of the horse-drawn Imperial war wagon, a fighting platform erects a defensive perimeter around the edge of a Steam Tank’s topside. As well as providing cover, it gives mounted engineers something to brace against, allowing them to stand atop the Steam Tank without falling off when it moves. 

Characters riding upon a fighting platform gain the benefit of hard cover (–30 to hit) from enemy attacks. Characters atop a fighting platform cannot make melee attacks against an enemy on foot unless they are wielding a weapon with Reach Long or greater, but gain +20 to hit when using those weapons. 

## **Open Top**
Removing the roof of a Steam Tank entirely exposes its crew to much greater dangers, but also permits the vehicle to mount indirect-fire weaponry that shoots in a high arc. This modification reduces the Steam Tank’s Toughness and Wounds by 20, and permits enemies to make attacks against its crew directly. Crew targeted by attacks from outside the Steam Tank gain the benefit of hard cover (–30 to hit). 

## **Boiler Modifications**
Each of these modifications applies tweaks to a Steam Tank’s boiler, its most essential component. 

## **Emergency Vent**
Instead of directing excess steam through the vehicle’s chimney (producing its signature ‘whistle’), this modification blasts superheated water out the Steam Tank’s flanks, leading to screaming, scalding death for any foe who gets too close. When a Character operating the Steam Tank’s engineering systems successfully Tests to reduce the Steam Tank’s Steam Points, all creatures within 3 yards of the vehicle (including those on top, but excluding those inside) suffer d10 Damage, modified by the defender’s Toughness Bonus, but ignoring deductions from Armour. 

## **Additional Boiler Carriage**
This modification, most renowned for its attachment to the Steam Tank Deliverance, couples a second carriage to the back of the vehicle. This carriages contains an overflow water tank, allowing the Steam Tank to consume greater quantities of steam power for the operation of more powerful weaponry. 

A Steam Tank with an additional boiler carriage raises its Maximum Pressure rating by +5, but reduces its movement speed (in and out of combat) by 50%. In addition, called shots against the Steam Tank’s boiler do not suffer a –20 penalty on attack Tests. 

## **Self-Destruct System**
This tool of last resort is used by vengeful engineer commanders who are determined to take as many foes as possible with them, and to protect the Empire’s technological secrets from falling into enemy hands. As an Action, a Character operating a Steam Tank’s engineering system may make a **Challenging (+0) Trade (Engineering)** Test to immediately inflict the Meltdown Steam Tank Mishap on the vehicle. The Damage inflicted by this Mishap is also inflicted on all creatures within 3 yards of the vehicle. 

**One of the most highly regarded roleplaying campaigns ever written, Every Gamer should play the Enemy Within**
